papers.title: OnlyAct: Extracting Action Representations from Foundation Models for World Models
papers.abstract: Video world models promise general-purpose interactive simulators, but their training is limited by action supervision: action labels are scarce, fragmented across incompatible specifications, and do not scale with the unlabeled video pretraining corpus. A common workaround jointly trains an action encoder to compress consecutive frames into a latent action and a decoder to reconstruct the next frame from the previous frame and that latent, forcing the latent to capture only new information. This has two limitations: learning the action space from scratch can limit generalization to unseen domains, and the bottleneck trades expressiveness for separation, with tighter settings losing nuance and looser ones risking scene leakage under domain shifts. We argue for a different starting point: rather than learning actions from scratch, we start from a pretrained foundation model (V-JEPA 2), whose embeddings of a frame pair already carry substantial action information after large-scale, diverse video pretraining. The remaining challenge is to extract the action while discarding the scene. We propose a label-free contrastive adaptation framework that pulls together frame pairs sharing the same motion under a different scene and pushes apart pairs from the same scene with different motion, reshaping the geometry of the pretrained space without imposing a reconstruction bottleneck. We introduce a unified evaluation protocol along three axes (action expressiveness, scene invariance, and action-conditioned video generation quality) across robot manipulation, camera navigation, game, and driving benchmarks, most of which are unseen during adaptation. Compared with annotation-free latent-action methods, our representations are substantially more expressive while matching their scene invariance, and they yield world models that transfer demonstrated actions to new scenes more faithfully.
papers.summary_cn: OnlyAct提出利用预训练视频基础模型V-JEPA 2提取动作表示，而不是从无标签视频中从零学习潜在动作。方法通过光流引导的跨场景正样本和同视频难负样本进行无标签对比适应，使嵌入突出运动信息并抑制场景信息，同时避免重建瓶颈造成的表达能力损失。实验覆盖机器人操作、相机导航、游戏和驾驶等领域，结果表明该表示具有更强的动作表达能力、相当的场景不变性，并能提升动作迁移和真实动作控制下的视频世界模型性能。
papers.contribution_cn: 1. 提出从预训练基础模型表示空间中提取动作、而非从零学习动作空间的新视角。2. 提出基于低秩适配器的无标签对比学习框架，利用光流引导的场景替换正样本和同视频难负样本，在无重建瓶颈的情况下实现动作与场景的解耦。3. 建立统一评测协议，从动作表达能力、场景不变性和动作条件视频生成质量三个方面进行评估。4. 在机器人、导航、游戏和驾驶基准上验证了更好的动作表达、跨场景动作迁移、视频生成可控性和真实动作微调效果。
papers.relevance_cn: 该工作直接面向动作条件视频世界模型和闭环交互式模拟：它从视频帧对中提取连续潜在动作，并将动作流输入自回归视频世界模型以预测后续帧。其动作迁移机制能够把演示视频中的动作施加到不同初始场景，适用于跨场景模拟和闭环控制；真实动作接口还支持用少量标注数据将机器人、游戏或驾驶动作映射到共享潜在动作空间。方法利用预训练视频时空先验，并通过对比适应增强跨领域泛化，与视频扩散、世界模型预训练和动作条件视频生成高度相关。不过论文重点不是实时生成、稀疏注意力、缓存复用或长视频流式生成。
papers.limitations_cn: 论文明确指出，光流引导的场景替换正样本仅适用于静态相机；对于移动相机、第一人称手持视频和驾驶视频，方法只能退化为对锚定帧对进行不同光度增强。方法仍需使用预训练基础模型、光流估计器和低秩适配，训练与推理成本及对光流质量的敏感性可能限制应用。真实动作控制还需要少量动作标注数据，并且世界模型需要针对目标领域微调。实验主要评估有限的视频域和数据集，论文未明确说明在超长视频、实时生成、流式推理、稀疏注意力或缓存复用方面的性能。
papers.abstract_cn: 视频世界模型有望成为通用交互式模拟器，但其训练受到动作监督的限制：动作标签稀缺，分散在彼此不兼容的规范中，并且无法随着无标签视频预训练语料的规模扩展。一种常见的解决方法是联合训练动作编码器和解码器：编码器将连续帧压缩为潜在动作，解码器根据前一帧和该潜在动作重建下一帧，从而迫使潜在表示只捕获新的信息。这种方法存在两个局限：从零开始学习动作空间可能限制对未见领域的泛化能力；此外，瓶颈在表达能力与动作—场景分离之间进行权衡，过强的压缩会损失细节，而过弱的压缩则可能在领域变化下引入场景信息。我们主张采用不同的出发点：不再从零开始学习动作，而是从预训练基础模型 V-JEPA 2 开始。该模型经过大规模、多样化的视频预训练，其对帧对的嵌入已经包含大量动作信息。这为学习更具泛化性的动作表示提供了基础。剩下的挑战是提取动作，同时丢弃场景信息。为此，我们提出一种无标签对比适应框架：将不同场景中具有相同运动的帧对拉近，并将同一场景中具有不同运动的帧对推远，从而在不施加重建瓶颈的情况下重塑预训练空间的几何结构。我们提出一个统一的评测协议，从三个维度考察动作表示——动作表达能力、场景不变性和动作条件视频生成质量——并在机器人操作、相机导航、游戏和驾驶基准上进行评估，其中大多数基准在适应阶段未被使用。与无需标注的潜在动作方法相比，我们的表示在保持相当场景不变性的同时具有显著更强的表达能力，并能使世界模型更忠实地将演示动作迁移到新场景中。

papers.title: Dynamics-Informed Action Learning for Goal-Conditioned Latent Planning
papers.abstract: Latent world models enable visual control by planning action sequences in compact representation spaces, but a gap remains between how latent dynamics are learned and how they are used for planning. First, teacher-forced training does not expose the dynamics model to the recursively predicted latent states encountered during planning. Second, sampling-based planners typically initialize action search from goal-agnostic proposals, without exploiting the action-conditioned dynamics learned by the world model. We introduce Dynamics-Informed Action Learning (DIAL) to bridge these two gaps. During training, rollout alignment exposes the forward model to its own autoregressive latent predictions, while multi-step inverse supervision trains a lightweight inverse dynamics head to infer actions from latent-state transitions. We further apply the inverse head to model-generated transitions with its parameters held fixed, encouraging predicted rollouts to retain action-relevant information. At test time, DIAL autoregressively couples the inverse and forward dynamics to construct a dynamics-informed action sequence toward the goal, which initializes the mean of the Cross-Entropy Method (CEM) proposal distribution. The subsequent CEM search then refines this initialization using the standard sampling and updating procedure. Experiments across four visual control benchmarks demonstrate that DIAL outperforms existing latent world models and planning baselines in both standard and long-horizon scenarios.
papers.summary_cn: 论文提出 DIAL，用于改进基于潜在世界模型的目标条件视觉规划。方法针对两个问题：教师强制训练与规划时自回归滚动之间存在分布不匹配，以及 CEM 通常使用与目标无关的初始动作分布。DIAL 通过轨迹对齐训练前向动力学，使其适应自身生成的潜在状态；通过多步逆动力学监督和对模型生成转移的逆动力学约束，保留潜在状态中的动作相关信息。规划时，逆动力学头根据当前预测状态和目标潜在状态生成动作，前向模型预测下一状态，由此形成的动作序列用于初始化 CEM 的均值，而不是直接执行。基于 LeWM 在 TwoRoom、PushT、Reacher 和 Cube 上的实验显示，DIAL 在 25 步和 50 步目标偏移下均取得更高成功率，尤其在搜索预算受限和长时域规划中优势明显。消融实验表明，模型生成轨迹上的动作可恢复性约束对性能提升尤为重要。
papers.contribution_cn: 1. 提出 DIAL，将潜在动力学学习与目标条件规划连接起来，利用学习到的逆动力学构造 CEM 的初始提议均值。2. 引入轨迹对齐训练，使前向动力学模型直接适应规划阶段的自回归潜在滚动。3. 引入多步逆动力学监督，从观测到的潜在状态转移中恢复起始动作，并通过固定参数的逆动力学头约束模型生成的状态转移保留动作相关信息。4. 在不增加 CEM 搜索预算、不改变后续标准采样与更新流程的情况下，实现由动力学信息引导的目标条件动作搜索。5. 在四个视觉控制基准、不同目标偏移和搜索预算下进行受控实验，证明方法在标准及长时域规划中的有效性。
papers.relevance_cn: 论文与研究重点高度相关。它研究动作条件潜在世界模型、目标条件视觉控制和闭环式模型预测规划；通过自回归前向动力学滚动处理长时域状态预测，并通过逆动力学将目标信息转化为动作序列。其主要机制属于动作条件视觉世界模型和潜在空间规划，而不是视频生成或视频扩散。DIAL 还直接涉及自回归生成、长时域规划、有限搜索预算下的高效推理以及模型生成状态的动作信息保持，但论文没有研究实时视频生成、扩散蒸馏、稀疏注意力或缓存复用。
papers.limitations_cn: 论文的实验主要限于四个视觉控制基准和离线数据集，结论对更复杂、更开放或真实世界环境的适用性尚未得到验证。方法依赖潜在表示、前向动力学和逆动力学头的准确性；论文指出，逆动力学生成的动作序列不一定构成准确的开放环路计划，因此仍需 CEM 进一步修正。长时域规划仍采用固定的有限规划视野和反复重规划，不能消除模型预测误差的累积。实验重点是成功率，论文未明确说明计算延迟、内存开销、扩展到更长视频序列的性能，以及与实时生成、扩散模型、稀疏注意力或缓存复用方法的比较。论文未明确说明在分布外目标、连续动作复杂性更高或观测噪声显著的情况下的鲁棒性。
papers.abstract_cn: 潜在世界模型通过在紧凑的表示空间中规划动作序列来实现视觉控制，但潜在动力学的学习方式与其在规划中的使用方式之间仍存在脱节。首先，教师强制训练不会使动力学模型接触到规划过程中遇到的递归预测潜在状态。其次，基于采样的规划器通常从与目标无关的候选方案开始动作搜索，没有利用世界模型所学习的动作条件动力学。我们提出动力学信息动作学习（Dynamics-Informed Action Learning，DIAL），以弥合这两个差距。在训练期间，轨迹对齐使前向模型接触自身自回归生成的潜在预测；多步逆动力学监督则训练一个轻量级逆动力学头，从潜在状态转移中推断动作。我们进一步将该逆动力学头应用于模型生成的状态转移，并固定其参数，从而促使预测轨迹保留与动作相关的信息。在测试时，DIAL 以自回归方式耦合逆动力学与前向动力学，构造一条朝向目标的、由动力学信息引导的动作序列，并用其初始化交叉熵方法（CEM）候选分布的均值。随后，CEM 使用标准的采样与更新过程对该初始化进行细化。在四个视觉控制基准上的实验表明，在标准场景和长时域场景中，DIAL 都优于现有的潜在世界模型和规划基线。

papers.title: WorldFoundry: Towards Unified Infrastructure for World Intelligence
papers.abstract: Visual generative models increasingly blur the line between synthesizing observations and simulating environments. Yet visual plausibility alone does not constitute successful world modeling: compelling outputs may lack persistent state, physical dynamics, or causally consistent responses to interactions. We define a generative world model as a predictive dynamical system that maintains a persistent, history-conditioned representation of an environment, updates that representation in response to actions or interventions, and generates temporally coherent trajectories that reflect outcomes under observed and counterfactual interventions. From this definition, we derive an intelligence-oriented framework spanning perceptual grounding, persistent state modeling, controllable transformation, dynamics-aware prediction, and closed-loop interaction. We present WorldFoundry, open-source infrastructure for reproducible inference and evaluation across video, 3D and 4D, embodied action, and interactive world systems. WorldFoundry unifies model and benchmark discovery, runtime and asset preparation, execution orchestration, artifact management, and interactive visualization, while modality-specific adapters preserve native inputs, execution semantics, output representations, and evaluation protocols. Explicit manifests, durable artifact contracts, and evidence-aware scorecards separate execution readiness from evaluative claims, making each claim traceable to its supporting artifacts. The catalog contains 270 model entries, 74 benchmarks, and 62 registered metric entries, with readiness and execution evidence recorded separately. WorldFoundry enables reproducible comparison of persistent, controllable dynamics across heterogeneous systems, advancing the field from perceptual synthesis toward measurable world intelligence.

papers.title: Semantically Aligned KV Cache Compression for Efficient Agentic Autoregressive Video Generation
papers.abstract: Agentic autoregressive video generation combines semantic planning, sequential generation, and visual verification for controllable synthesis. Growing visual histories enlarge the key-value (KV) cache, increasing memory use and attention costs across candidate rollouts. Existing compression methods primarily optimize individual generators without the planner's semantic constraints, risking low priority for states supporting requested attributes or actions. We introduce SemanticKV, a training-free method for semantically aligned KV cache compression. To our knowledge, SemanticKV is the first KV cache compression method for agentic autoregressive video generation that explicitly uses planner-extracted semantic constraints to guide retention. Text cross-attention identifies constraint-related video positions, whose self-attention queries are collected into separate groups. Attention weights are averaged within each group and maximized across groups, giving each cached entry a high score when strongly used by any represented constraint. A single top-k selection retains high-scoring entries under the memory budget, leaving their keys, values, and positions unchanged. For fixed query groups and equal entry costs, this selection minimizes an additive upper bound on worst-group discarded attention. The method operates independently within each candidate without retraining or additional video generations. We evaluate four AR video backbones on three benchmarks for 5-, 30-, and 60-second generation. On Causal Forcing at a compression ratio of 0.7, SemanticKV obtains a VBench Total Score of 84.10, compared with 84.05 for the strongest compressed baseline and 83.99 for Full KV. It achieves a 1.22x speedup over Full KV and reduces KV-cache memory from 6.04 GB to 1.81 GB, a 3.35x reduction.
papers.summary_cn: Agentic autoregressive video generation combines semantic planning, sequential generation, and visual verification for controllable synthesis.
papers.contribution_cn: We introduce SemanticKV, a training-free method for semantically aligned KV cache compression.

papers.title: Few-Step Streaming Video Generation via Condition Shifting
papers.abstract: Few-step sampling reduces the cost of streaming video generation. Distribution Matching Distillation (DMD) supervises few-step generators with a separate fake-score network, which adds training memory and computation and must track the evolving generator. We extend APEX to streaming video by using condition shifting to estimate the velocity field of the generated distribution within the generator. The original text condition selects generation, while a shifted condition selects fake estimation using the same parameters. This removes the independent fake network while retaining S2-Avatar's frozen reference teacher, Self-Replay Forcing, and perceptual regularization. We evaluate APEX on 180-second videos using three backbone evaluations per block and a one-step spatial Refiner, with a 70-case human study and a 320-case StreamAV-Bench comparison. Compared with S2-Avatar, APEX achieves higher video instruction fulfillment on the Progressive track (3.856 versus 3.831) and higher visual aesthetics across both tracks (0.641898 versus 0.632606). Human raters favor APEX most strongly on instruction following, with +30.0% net preference, followed by consistency and video quality at +4.3% each. Motion quality favors S2-Avatar, audiovisual synchronization is predominantly tied, and usability is unchanged. Separate measurements under matched training settings show 4.4% lower peak allocated GPU memory per GPU and 9.2% shorter mean iteration time than DMD.
papers.summary_cn: Few-step sampling reduces the cost of streaming video generation.

papers.title: Tiresias: Towards Language-Conditioned World Models
papers.abstract: World models enable planning through internal simulation, while natural language provides intuitive task specification. Yet, language-conditioned world modeling remains fragmented across domains with disparate action spaces, datasets, and evaluation protocols. We introduce LCWM, a shared task that maps an initial agent-view observation and a language instruction to an action sequence that fulfills the instruction. Its accompanying benchmark, LCWM-Bench, integrates 15 datasets across navigation, robotics, 3D gaming, and driving under a shared action interface and evaluation protocol, pairing 142,987 episodes with 428,961 instructions in three styles. We further propose Tiresias, an agent that plans via selective imagination: a language-conditioned diffusion policy generates candidate trajectories, a trajectory ranker shortlists them, and a video-pretrained world model imagines their visual consequences. A visual ranker evaluates these rollouts, complementing trajectory scores to select the final plan. Tiresias achieves competitive planning and imagination performance on LCWM-Bench. Ablations demonstrate the complementary benefits of trajectory ranking and visual verification, while experiments with alternative proposal methods show that the trained rankers remain effective beyond our diffusion policy. Together, LCWM-Bench and Tiresias provide a unified evaluation setting and an effective starting point for studying language-guided planning through world models.

papers.title: DexForesight: Grounding Dexterous Policies with Implicit Spatial Foresight
papers.abstract: Dexterous manipulation requires rich spatial foresight over both the surrounding scene and the robot hand. Existing world-action models often acquire such predictive knowledge through explicit future prediction. We introduce DexForesight, a framework that learns spatial foresight implicitly by injecting dynamics-aware world representations into the latent space of a dexterous policy. During training, DexForesight learns an action-conditioned spatial world model from offline scene depth, kinematic hand geometry, and demonstration trajectories. The world model predicts 3D hand-point motion and visual feature changes, capturing both articulated hand dynamics and scene changes under demonstrated actions, including the motion of fingers occluded from the cameras. We then freeze the world model and align policy queries with its predictive world queries, transferring the learned spatial dynamics into policy latents and using them to condition action generation. At deployment, only the policy is retained, operating on RGB observations, language, and robot state without depth input or explicit future prediction. On 11 DexJoCo simulation tasks, DexForesight improves the overall success rate of the base policy from 49.4% to 60.5%. On three real-robot dexterous manipulation tasks, DexForesight achieves 58.3% success, compared with 50.0% for the strongest baseline. Project page https://dexforesight.github.io/

papers.title: LO-World: Unified BEV Latent Modeling for Joint 4D Occupancy and LiDAR Forecasting
papers.abstract: LiDAR point clouds and 3D semantic occupancy represent two distinct modalities capturing fine-grained metric geometry and dense volumetric semantics, respectively, holding natural potential for mutual complementarity. However, existing world models typically forecast these modalities independently or cascade them heuristically, missing the opportunity for reciprocal cross-modal regularization. To address this, we propose \textbf{LO-World}, a unified 4D world model that forecasts both modalities within a shared BEV latent space. This single-stream formulation enables dense semantics and metric geometry to mutually reinforce each other, while eliminating multi-pipeline redundancy. Specifically, LO-World couples an efficient hybrid range-voxel autoencoder with a flow-matching generator that caches historical context to reduce iterative sampling latency. Extensive experiments demonstrate that LO-World outperforms prior state-of-the-art baselines, improving occupancy forecasting IoU by 10.9% and reducing LiDAR Chamfer Distance by 30.1%. Meanwhile, it sustains a real-time throughput exceeding $25$~FPS on a single RTX 4090. Our code is available at https://github.com/lzzzzzm/LO-World.
papers.summary_cn: LiDAR point clouds and 3D semantic occupancy represent two distinct modalities capturing fine-grained metric geometry and dense volumetric semantics, respectively, holding natural potential for mutual complementarity.

papers.title: ProTEUS: A mutation-resolved world model for closed-loop protein evolution
papers.abstract: Protein engineering requires navigating rugged fitness landscapes, where small sequence changes can produce large functional differences, but experimental screening can only sample a small fraction of sequence space. Thus, a central challenge is to efficiently traverse the large combinatorial space of mutations in silico. We introduce ProTEUS, a mutation-resolved world model for closed-loop protein evolution. Pretrained on deep mutational scanning assays, ProTEUS learns a joint representation of sequence, evolutionary, and structural information using MutationFormer, a mutation-biased attention architecture. Variants are represented as states in this joint latent space, and mutations define actions whose functional consequences are predicted. To support exploration of many mutants, we developed a fast, physics-constrained all-atom predictor that utilizes explicit geometric constraint enforcement to achieve >10 fold increase in speed than AlphaFold3 with guaranteed physical validity. Lastly, ProTEUS refines its prediction and understanding of protein activity through closed loop experimental feedback to guide evolution toward a desired phenotype. ProTEUS surpasses established models in both zero-shot and supervised fine-tuning mutation prediction tasks. We experimentally demonstrate its utility in two closed-loop multi-objective engineering campaigns on aldehyde dehydrogenase and levansucrase, yielding variants with >10 fold higher activity than wild type. ProTEUS provides a world-model framework that connects virtual evaluation of mutational outcomes with experimental learning for efficient protein evolution.

papers.title: Mitigating SM-Level Load Imbalance in 3D Gaussian Splatting on GPUs
papers.abstract: 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) enables photorealistic, real-time rendering on commodity GPUs and is increasingly adopted in generative world models and autonomous driving simulators. However, existing optimizations rely on algorithmic changes that often require retraining, or on specialized accelerators that lack flexibility across evolving 3DGS variants. In this paper, we identify a fundamental inefficiency in GPU-based 3DGS rendering: severe SM-level load imbalance caused by uneven workloads across screen tiles. This imbalance creates a long execution tail, leaving most SMs idle while a few process computationally intensive tiles, particularly in large-scale urban scenes. To address this, we present a software-defined GPU scheduling approach that mitigates the execution tail. Our approach uses a persistent kernel to schedule heavy tiles first and selectively chunks outlier tiles across multiple CTAs. A lightweight per-frame policy determines when and how much to chunk using tile statistics already available in the rendering pipeline. Our approach requires neither retraining nor specialized hardware and can be applied orthogonally to existing optimizations across diverse 3DGS variants. Averaged per scene, it accelerates alpha blending by up to 2.93x on a large-scale urban scene, and by up to 5.6x on its most imbalanced frames, while retaining the original alpha blending formulation.
